lead_headline: Lost Coffee opens sixth Colorado location in Arvada while Samir restaurant surfaces in Congress Park—115 active leads in pipeline

restaurant.blurb: 2 new leads today: Lost Coffee (sixth Colorado location, Arvada) and Samir Mediterranean/Afghan (Congress Park, replacing Rico's Pizzeria). Active pipeline: 115 leads (59 openings, 56 closures).

foreclosure.blurb: $6.1M Douglas County property at 18901 Longs Way leads this week's slate — the sole filing exceeding $4M threshold. Auction scheduled Thursday.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today marks Monday's first filing drought since early March. Weekly volume holds at 20 applications — double the pre-March baseline — led by restaurant/tavern expansions in Jefferson Park, RiNo, and Highlands. Notable: Red Lotus Den food hall (Westminster) and The Couloir après bar (Overland) filed for tavern licenses ahead of summer openings. Zero status changes suggests State processing backlog remains clear following March's enforcement wave.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions yesterday lifts the 7-day total to 41 across 10 sources — down 20% from last week's 51-mention baseline. Instagram (10) edges Denver Post (9) for weekly dominance, followed by Hoodline (6) and Facebook (5). Week-over-week contraction marks second consecutive decline after mid-April's 54-mention peak, suggesting development news cycle fatigue. Notable pickups: Morning Story Chapter 11 filing (Hoodline), Denver Pavilions consultant report (Reddit), and tipped wage debate coverage across social platforms.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) holds MTD at +18 (+0.9/day), 90-day net at +141. This week's +10 net (15 new, 5 canceled) matches last week's +11 performance despite 38% lower acquisition volume (15 vs 24 new) — the convergence stems from 62% fewer cancellations (5 vs 13), suggesting Sunday-Monday churn volatility has stabilized. Recent 14-day pattern shows Monday flatlines bracketing stronger midweek conversion windows: April 7-13 delivered +13 net before April 14-20's choppy sequence settled at +5. MTD's +0.9/day pace continues trailing YTD's +1.4/day benchmark as late-month momentum stalls, though sustained low-churn weekends signal healthier retention baseline entering May.
